title: Concatenation of Consecutive Binary Numbers
statement: Write the numbers `1, 2, ..., n` in binary (without leading zeros) and join them end to end, in that order, into one long bit string. Read that bit string as a binary number and return its value modulo `10^9 + 7`.
notes:
## Intuition

Appending a number `i` that has `length` bits to the end of a binary value shifts that value left by `length` places and then adds `i`. So the answer can be built one number at a time without ever forming the long string, reducing modulo `10^9 + 7` after each step. The only extra fact needed is the bit length of `i`, which grows by one exactly when `i` is a power of two, and a power of two is the one case where `i & (i - 1)` is 0. Building the whole string and reading it bit by bit also works, but handles every one of its roughly n·log2(n) bits instead of one step per number.

## Approach

1. Keep `result` (the value so far, reduced modulo `MOD`) and `length` (bits in the current number).
2. For each `i` from 1 to `n`, if `i & (i - 1)` is 0 then `i` is a power of two and needs one more bit, so increase `length`.
3. Shift `result` left by `length` bits (multiply by `1 << length`), add `i`, and take the remainder modulo `MOD`.
4. Return `result`.

## Example 1, step by step

With `n = 1`, the loop runs once: `i = 1` and `1 & 0 = 0`, so `length` becomes 1, and `result = 0 * 2 + 1 = 1`. The answer is `1`. Carrying on as in Example 2: `i = 2` is a power of two, so `length = 2` and `result = 1 * 4 + 2 = 6` (`110`); `i = 3` keeps `length = 2`, giving `6 * 4 + 3 = 27` (`11011`).

## Complexity

- Time: O(n): one constant-time step per number.
- Space: O(1).

## Pitfalls

- Never build the real string or number: its value has over a million bits for large `n`.
- In JavaScript, `result << length` works on 32-bit integers and overflows; multiply by `1 << length` instead (the product stays below 2^47). In Java or C use a 64-bit integer.
- Reduce modulo `10^9 + 7` on every step, not only at the end.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `MOD` | the modulus `10^9 + 7` |
| `result` | value of the joined bits of `1..i`, modulo `MOD` |
| `length` | number of bits in `i` |
| `i` | the number being appended |

narration.3: The value of the joined bits so far; nothing joined yet.
narration.4: How many bits the current number has.
narration.5: Append the numbers 1 to n in order.
narration.6: i & (i - 1) clears the lowest set bit, so it is 0 exactly when i is a power of two.
narration.7: A power of two needs one more bit than the number before it.
narration.9: Shift the value left by length bits, append i in the freed bits, and reduce.
narration.11: The reduced value of the whole concatenation.
